title: Evaluation of long-chain fatty acid respiration in neonatal mouse cardiomyocytes using SeaHorse instrument
protocol: Anesthetize the pups according to your protocol approval.
Sterilize the abdomen with antiseptic solution.
Euthanize mouse pups by decapitation using sharp scissors.
Collect the heart while it is still beating.
Place hearts in ice-cold CMF Hank’s Balanced Salt Solution (HBSS), pH 7.4, in a small petri dish on an ice bed.
Remove extra-cardiac tissues and blood from the hearts.
Cut each heart into 2–3 longitudinal pieces.
Transfer heart sections to 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes containing 450 μL of HBSS.
Label the tubes accordingly.
Keep the tubes on ice until the end of the collection process.
Resuspend the trypsin vial in 2 mL of ice-cold sterile HBSS to obtain a 500 μg/mL solution.
Incubate the tubes for at least 10–12 hours at 4°C (fridge).
Transfer the tissue and solution into a 10 mL tube under a sterile hood.
Add 100 μL of Trypsin inhibitor per 500 μL of tissue-containing solution.
Incubate for 5 minutes at 37°C.
Resuspend collagenase in 5 mL of pre-warm Leibovitz L-15 medium.
Add 250 μL of collagenase per 500 μL of tissue-containing solution.
Incubate at 37°C under slow rotation (2–4 rpm) for 45 minutes to one hour.
Prepare a complete medium containing Leibovitz L-15 medium with 10% horse serum, 5% fetal bovine serum, and 1% penicillin-streptomycin.
Pre-warm the medium at 37°C in a water bath.
Triturate cells at least 10 times under sterile conditions using a wide-mouth pipette or regular 10 mL pipette to avoid air bubbles and high-speed pipetting.
Pre-wash a 40 μm strainer with 1 mL of L15 culture medium.
Strain the triturated cells through the pre-washed strainer, washing it with an additional 1 mL of medium.
Repeat straining the cells one more time.
Rinse the strainer with 2 mL of medium to ensure all cells are collected.
Pre-plate the cell-containing medium in non-coated 35 mm² dishes and incubate at 37°C for 1 hour undisturbed.
Gently collect the suspended cells without washing too vigorously, as this may detach fibroblasts.
Spin the collected cells at 150 g for 5 minutes at 21°C to pellet them.
Resuspend the cell pellet in appropriate volume of L-15 complete medium.
Seed 3–4 mouse pup heart equivalents onto a 35 mm diameter dish.
Pre-coat the plate with Poly-Lysine to improve adhesion if necessary.
Leave the seeded cells undisturbed between 24 and 48 hours.
Trypsinize and split cardiomyocytes into new plates after 24–48 hours of seeding.
Replace seeding medium with culture medium upon splitting.
Treat cells isolated from transgenic mouse models with 4OH-tamoxifen for 4 consecutive days if required.
Transfer the cells to SeaHorse 8-well plates.
Ensure that SeaHorse plates and sensors match your SeaHorse Flux Analyzer instrument.
Remove the seeding medium from the cells.
Wash the cells gently with sterile D-PBS.
Apply 1 mL of Trypsin EDTA 0.05% for a 35 mm diameter dish to trypsinize the cells.
Incubate at 37°C for 5 minutes.
Collect the cells after incubation.
Spin the collected cells at 150 g for 5 minutes at room temperature (19°C–21°C).
Discard the supernatant from the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL of complete culture medium (DMEM – Horse Serum 5% - Fetal Bovine Serum 10% - Penicillin/Streptomycin 1%).
Prepare a 1:10 dilution of the resuspended cells in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Load 10 μL of the 1:10 diluted cell suspension into a counting chamber of a hematocytometer or an automatic cell counter.
Estimate the concentration of undiluted cell suspension based on the count.
Calculate the volume needed to load 25,000 cells in 100 μL of medium.
Prepare the appropriate dilution of the cell suspension accordingly.
Note the requirement for BSA-incubated and Palmitate-incubated wells in presence or absence of etomoxir for lipid metabolism estimation.
Incubate cells with appropriate conditions including pharmacological drug incubation or tamoxifen-induced gene disruption as needed.
Prepare Seahorse miniplate for a LCFA oxidation assay according to schematic representation (A).
Assign plate groups for the assay, ensuring cell-free background wells are included per plate (Figure 2A).
Place plates in an incubator at 37°C/5% CO2.
Leave plates for additional 24 hours or at least 12 hours for cell seeding.
Optional: Pre-coat SeaHorse miniplates with poly-lysine or collagen for at least 1 hour before seeding cells.
Change medium every two days to maintain cells in culture for up to one week.
Dilute 4OH-tamoxifen at 100 nM in complete maintenance medium.
Gently wash cells with D-PBS.
Replace medium with 200 μL of fresh medium containing tamoxifen.
Check the viability of the cells after 24 hours (Day 1 post-tamoxifen).
Replace the medium with fresh medium containing 100 nM of 4OH-tamoxifen at Day 2 or Day 3, and every 2-3 days if longer incubation is needed.
Ascertained the efficiency of gene disruption in neonatal cardiomyocytes (NMCMs) before running any Seahorse plate experiment with a new transgenic mouse line.
Isolated DNA for genotyping the "floxed" alleles of the transgene of interest.
Performed RNA isolation and RT-qPCR for the mRNA coding the protein of interest.
Conducted Western blot analysis for the protein of interest.
Noticed changes in beating rate when metabolism or Ca2+ cycling are impacted.
Replace medium with substrate-limited medium: MEM + with 1% serum, 1% antibiotics, 1% Glutamine, and 1% L-Carnitine.
Incubate cells in a regular incubator at 18.6% O2, 5% CO2, and 37°C.
Prepare an aliquot of SeaHorse Calibrant Buffer (5 mL) and place it in a non-CO2 37°C environment for at least 12 hours.
Under a sterile cell culture hood, remove the top part of the cartridge.
Place the removed top part upside down on your sterile bench.
Add 200 μL of sterile distilled water into each well of the cartridge utility plate.
Add 400 μL of sterile water in the compartments (moats) on each side of the utility plate to prevent evaporation.
Place the green part of the cartridge back onto the utility plate, so the sensors are fully submerged.
Incubate the cartridges at 37°C in a Non-CO2 incubator.
Wrap the cartridges with aluminum foil or parafilm to prevent overnight evaporation.
Store rehydrated cartridges short-term at 4°C up to 24–48 h before use, keeping them wrapped in parafilm and aluminum foil.
Discard any leftover Calibrant buffer.
Turn on the SeaHorse Flux Analyzer to ensure it is set at 37°C for the experiment.
Prepare the program using the Wave software and save the file onto a USB drive used for data collection.
Add FCCP working solution into the injection port C if needed, and include an additional injection and measurement in your program.
Prepare a layout of your miniplate(s) indicating the treatment of your cells.
Prepare FAO medium up to 10–20 mL and filter it with a 0.20 μm filter gauge.
Wash the wells of the plate (containing cells) twice with 200-300 μL of FAO medium under a sterile hood.
Add 130 μL of FAO medium in each well.
Incubate the plate in a Non-CO2 37°C incubator for 60 min.
Remove the water from the wells of the utility plate and replace it with pre-warm aliquoted SeaHorse Calibrant Buffer.
Place the cartridge back to the Non-CO2 incubator and incubate for 45-60 min.
Prepare the SeaHorse reagent working solutions.
Resuspend the pouches as per manufacturer instructions if using Agilent Mito Stress Kit.
Pre-warm Palmitate and BSA stock solutions at 52°C.
Mix 100 μL of Palmitate 10 mM with 200 μL of 1 mM BSA in room temperature FAO medium (final volume = 1 mL).
Mix 200 μL of 1 mM BSA stock with 800 μL of FAO medium.
Dilute Oligomycin at a ratio of 1:100 in FAO medium for intermediate dilution.
Prepare working solution by mixing 48 μL of the intermediate oligomycin dilution with 252 μL of FAO medium.
Load 25 μL/well (1 μM per well) for Oligomycin.
Dilute FCCP in FAO medium at a ratio of 24 μL stock solution to 900 μL FAO medium for intermediate dilution.
Prepare working solution by mixing 200 μL of the intermediate FCCP dilution with 800 μL of FAO medium.
Load 25 μL/well (16 μM per well) for FCCP.
Dilute Rotenone in FAO medium at a ratio of 10 μL stock solution to 990 μL FAO medium for intermediate dilution #1.
Further dilute Rotenone from intermediate dilution #1 by mixing 1:100 in FAO medium for intermediate dilution #2.
Prepare working solution by mixing 60 μL of intermediate dilution #2 with 240 μL of FAO medium.
Load 25 μL/well (0.5 μM per well) for Rotenone.
Load the injection ports of a pre-equilibrated cartridge with oligomycin.
Load the injection ports of a pre-equilibrated cartridge with FCCP.
Load the injection ports of a pre-equilibrated cartridge with Rotenone/Antimycin A.
Place the cartridge on the SeaHorse Flux Analyzer.
Start the program on the SeaHorse Flux Analyzer.
Launch the calibration step according to instrument instructions.
Add 20 μL of Etomoxir solution in the wells designated for Etomoxir treatment.
Prepare Etomoxir solution by mixing 5 μL of stock Etomoxir (30 mM) with 745 μL of FAO medium.
Add 25 μL of BSA-conjugated-Palmitate working solution to the wells.
Start the program after loading the cell plate into the instrument.
Export the dataset file using a USB key at the end of the experiment.
Load a new cartridge for calibration if starting a second run is needed.
Retrieve your plate from the SeaHorse instrument.
Remove FAO medium from the plate.
Wash the plate gently twice with PBS.
Add 10–20 μL of cell lysis buffer to the plate.
Estimate protein concentration via a Bradford or BCA assay.
Optional: Run a Western blot using 5–10 μL of cell lysate if necessary.
If performing a Western blot, add protease/phosphatase inhibitor cocktail to the cell lysis buffer.
Place the plate on an ice-bed immediately after the SeaHorse experiment.
